title: Assetized Prompt Components — mini PRD + notes
content:
TL;DR: sketching an idea to treat discrete prompt fragments as first-class versioned assets that can be composed at runtime. Goals: faster developer iteration, reuse across teams, caching/prefetch opportunities, safer rollouts, and clearer telemetry mapping from user outcomes back to prompt building blocks.

Context / motivation
- We have lots of repeated prompt patterns across customers (system messages, role templates, instruction postprocessing snippets, few-shot examples, safety filters).
- Engineers copy/paste and slightly tweak; hard to audit, test, or measure incremental changes.
- If prompts are assetized (named, versioned, composable), we can: 1) reuse and share best-of-breed templates, 2) enable targeted A/B for a small component instead of whole prompt, 3) prefetch/coldstart caches for commonly-used fragments, 4) attribute quality regressions to particular components.

Primary user personas
- ML engineer embedding a safety filter snippet into multiple chat flows. Wants versioning + rollback.
- Product engineer composing onboarding flows from a prompt library (language-specific). Wants clear UX and fast iteration.
- Platform/SRE wants to pre-warm KV cache or batching for commonly-requested static parts.
- Solutions engineers / customers want ability to pin a component to a private repo/namespace in Private deployment.

Core idea (very rough)
- Asset: a small, named prompt fragment with metadata. Types: system, instruction, example (few-shot), post-filter, slot-template (mustache-like), function-schema.
- Each asset has: id, name, version, owner, visibility (org/private/public), validation tests (unit prompts + expected checks), tags, canonical language variants, and optional precompiled token footprint/expected length distribution.
- Composition layer: a light DSL (or JSON spec) that lists an ordered sequence of assets + inline content + dynamic slots (session variables). Example composition: [system: onboarding-v2, slots: user_profile, examples: order-cancel-samples@v3, instruction: summarize@v1].
- Runtime: compose assets into a final prompt just-in-time, or compile to a cached compiled prompt for hot paths.

User stories
- As an ML engineer I can create asset 'safety-filter-v1', attach unit evals (prompt->expected false/true), and publish it to my org so product teams can include it.
- As a product engineer I can reference assets by name+semver in my route config and see a preview of the rendered prompt with sample session data.
- As SRE I can see which assets are used most (per route/model) and opt to pre-compile or cache them to reduce per-request tokenization overhead.
- As a platform admin I can roll out asset changes via canary/percentage-based rollout targeting specific routes or user cohorts.

Acceptance criteria (MVP-ish)
- Create/update/delete assets in the Console and via API (crud).
- Basic composition: route-level composition spec supports referencing up to 10 assets and dynamic slots.
- Versioning: assets are immutable once published (publish creates a new semantic version).
- Preview: Console shows a rendered preview (with example slot values).
- Telemetry: we track asset usage per request (asset_id + version) and surface top-10 used assets in a route dashboard.
- Safety tests: support attaching 1–5 small unit-evals to an asset that run on publish and on model change.

Nice-to-haves / stretch
- Language variants per asset (auto-translate suggestions).
- Community/public asset catalog (curated by Redwood) with opt-in copying.
- Precompilation: pre-tokenize and pre-KV-cache compiled prompts for <50 top assets per region/model.
- Asset A/B: built-in rollout engine to split traffic by asset version.

Open questions / risks
- Security & data leakage: if assets include sensitive examples, how do we prevent cross-tenant leakage? Need strict org-scoping and possibly labeling for 'no-cache' assets.
- UX surface: Console complexity — how to avoid overwhelming product teams with asset primitives? Maybe start with two modal types: 'system' (monolithic) and 'slot-templates' (structured).
- Performance tradeoffs: composing at request time adds overhead; precompilation/caching reduces flexibility. Need to model cost delta.
- Schema flexibility: do we adopt a typed schema (YAML/JSON) for composition or a simple ordered list? Simpler = faster adoption.
- Migration: how to migrate existing inline prompts in customer routes to reference assets? Manual mapping, plus a tool to detect identical fragments and propose asset creation.

Quick API sketch (very rough)
- POST /v1/assets {name, type, content, owner_team, visibility, tests[], tags[]} -> returns asset_id + version
- GET /v1/assets/{asset_id} -> metadata + versions list
- POST /v1/compositions {route_id, assets:[{asset_id,version,slot_bindings}], inline_overrides:...} -> attach to route
- Runtime: request includes composition_id or explicit asset references; server composes at tokenization stage.

Console ideas (wireframe notes)
- Library view: filter by type, tag, last-used, owner. Quick preview on hover shows token count and sample render.
- Asset detail: version timeline, tests tab (run tests), telemetry tab (requests last 7/30d), access controls.
- Compose route flow: drag assets into ordered list, bind session variables, preview.
- Migration helper page: shows inline prompt clusters that are identical/similar and suggests creating assets from clusters.

Telemetry & metrics to validate impact
- Adoption: number of routes referencing assets, average assets per route.
- Reuse: unique routes per asset (higher = more reuse).
- Latency/cost impact: compare P95 latency and tokenization CPU before/after precompilation.
- QA velocity: time from change->deploy when changing an asset vs changing an entire prompt (survey/qual).
- Regression detection: number of regressions traced to asset vs to model change.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0 (internal): prototype with 1 product team (onboarding flows). Manual mapping only, no precompilation.
- Phase 1 (limited): add Console CRUD, basic composition, telemetry. Invite 3–5 teams.
- Phase 2 (org-wide): add versioned rollouts, basic precompile for top assets, migration tool.
- Phase 3 (public): curated Redwood asset catalog, public examples, add language variants.

Experiment ideas
- Precompile experiment: precompile top 25 assets for route X and measure latency and tail CPU.
- A/B at component level: swap safety-filter-v1 vs v2 for 20% traffic and track QA / hallucination metrics.
- Reuse incentive: demonstrate cost reductions by encouraging reuse for common system messages (measure tokens saved).

Notes to self / todos
- Talk to Maya about unit-eval infra and whether we can reuse existing micro-eval harness.
- Check infra limits: how many compiled prompt cache entries per serving node is safe? Ask infra team.
- Sketch Console mockups (low-fidelity) and get quick feedback from Solutions Eng.
- Draft Confluence PRD with proposed API and data model.

Fringe ideas (putting here so I don't forget)
- Signing assets: allow cryptographic signing for Private deployments so customer-owned assets can be audited.
- Asset diffs: show token-level diff between versions and estimated cost delta.
- Auto-suggest: detect repeated inline text across routes and suggest turning into an asset.

Bottom line: this feels like a high-leverage, medium-effort platform feature. Start small (CRUD + composer + telemetry) and iterate toward precompilation and rollouts. Prioritize safety tests and scoping to prevent leakage.

Random brainstorming fragments / one-liners
- "Treat prompts like infra: small, composable, versioned building blocks."
- "Ship one asset catalog export so customers can diff their private assets across environments."
- "We should be explicit about token overhead vs. reuse wins — build a small cost estimator into the Console."

End of scratchpad.
